3. Respondent No.2, the Bank opposed the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the Writ petition contending, inter alia that bank filed Money Execution. Case No.7 of 1995 which was dismissed on 14-5-2001 and thereafter, the Bank filed second execution case on 5-8-2002 for recovery of its decretal dues within the period of limitation as per provision of Limitation Act and the Ain. Therefore, the execution proceeding as well as the order for issuing of war- rant of arrest is lawful and the rule is thus, liable to be discharged. 

 4. The petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit stating that the first execution case was filed on 27-11-1995 before the Adalat for execution of the decree dated 1-8-1991 and therefore, the first execution case was barred by limitation under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. As the first execution case is time barred, all other subsequent application for execution of the said decree is also time barred and, as such, the execution proceeding is liable to be struck down. 

 5. Mr Mohammad Hedayet Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner invites our attention to the information slip (Annexure-H to the Supplementary Affidavit) and submits that the suit was decreed on 1-8-1991 and the first execution case for execution of the decree was filed on 27-11-1995 and, as such, the first execution case having been filed beyond the period of 3 years as required under Article 182 of the Limitation Act was barred by limitation. He next submits that the first execution case was disallowed on 14-5-2001 and the second execution case was then filed by the decree-holder-Bank on 5-8-2002. He lastly submits that the first execution case being barred by limitation the subsequent Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 is also barred by limitation and the entire proceeding of the Money Execution Case is thus, liable to be declared to be without authority. 

 6. Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque the learned Advocate for the Bank submits that as the record of Money Decree Execution Case No.7 of 1995 has been destroyed, the Bank is unable to ascertain as to whether the first execution case was filed earlier or whether any application for condonation of delay was filed in the first execution case and, as such, it cannot be presumed that the first execution case is barred by limitation and therefore, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 8. It transpires from the information slip (Annexure-H to the supplementary affidavit) that Money Decree Execution Case No. 7 of 1995 was filed on 27-11-1995 and the said execution case was disallowed on 14-5-2001 as found from the filing Register. It further transpires from the ex parte judgment and decree (Annexure-B and B I to the Writ petition) that Money Suit No. 27 of 1990 was decreed ex parte on 1-8-1991 and decree was drawn up the signed on 10-8-1991. Therefore, it is evident from the materials on record that first execution case was filed beyond the period of 3 years. Thus, the first execution case was barred by limitation in view of the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act. As the first execution case was barred by limitation, we are of the view that subsequent Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of2002 for execution case of the said decree is also barred by limitation. 

 "We have gone through the available materials particularly the judgment of the executing Court, appellate Court and also of the High Court Division, it appears that the Second Appeal was dismissed on 15-7-1982 and it is well settled that the decree holder may then proceed with the earlier execution proceeding but a separate proceeding initiated which is admittedly barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. Before this Court or even before the High Court Division the petitioners failed to produce any paper showing the facts of earlier execution proceeding. It is well settled that the decree may be executed within 12 years from the date of decree and that in the present case from 15-7-1982 on which date the Second Appeal was dismissed but in proceeding with such decree the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act is to be followed. The High Court Division found that this provision of law has not been followed and accordingly the proceeding is barred under Limitation Act. Mr Quasem, learned Advocate though tried frantically to convince us that the present case is not barred by limitation but we fail to agree with the submission in view of the fact that the Second Appeal was dismissed on 15-7-1982 and there is non-compliance of the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act. On consideration of the available materials we hold that the High Court Division has not committed any illegality and wrong in making the rule absolute." 

 11. From the discussions made hereinbefore, it is evident that the proceeding of Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka being barred by limitation is unlawful.
